title: U.S. House · North Carolina's 12th District
area: Mostly the city of Charlotte and surrounding parts of Mecklenburg County.

context.text: Incumbent Alma Adams defeated one Democratic primary challenger with 78.9% of the vote. Jack Codiga won the Republican primary with 67.4% of the vote over one challenger.

summary.text: Alma Adams is the Democratic incumbent for North Carolina's 12th Congressional District, a former art professor who has represented the Charlotte-based district since 2015 and serves on the House Agriculture and Education and Workforce Committees.

background.text: Earned her B.S. and M.S. from North Carolina A&T University and her Ph.D. from Ohio State University.
Worked as an art professor at Bennett College before her election to Congress.

Serves on the House Committee on Agriculture (Conservation, Research, and Biotechnology; Nutrition and Foreign Agriculture) and the Committee on Education and the Workforce for the 2025-2026 Congress; previously served on the Committee on Financial Services (2019-2022).

record.text: Assigned to the House Committee on Agriculture and the Committee on Education and the Workforce for the 2025-2026 Congress.

candidates.name: Jack Codiga
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary with 67.4% of the vote.

summary.text: Jack Codiga is the Republican nominee for North Carolina's 12th Congressional District, a finance professional running on ending the Federal Reserve and a return to a gold- and silver-backed currency.

background.text: Earned a high school diploma from Scotts Valley High School and a bachelor's degree in finance from Santa Clara University's Leavey School of Business.
Career experience includes working as a finance professional.

priorities.text: Supports abolishing the Federal Reserve and returning currency control to the U.S. Treasury backed by gold and silver, which he says would address the rising cost of housing and other basics.
priorities.quote: I support ending the Federal Reserve, which currently controls our money and oversees a banking system where new money is created through loans. Control of our currency should return to the U.S. Treasury, with gold and silver once again serving as money.

priorities.text: Supports opening up primary elections so more candidates can compete, through a majority-winner or top-two runoff system.
priorities.quote: One of my priorities is giving voters more real choices by opening up the primary system so more candidates can compete. This would require either a majority winner or a runoff between the top two candidates.

priorities.text: Says immigration is his most passionate policy area and supports deporting violent criminals and those who abuse government programs.
priorities.quote: We need a clear approach that starts with deporting violent criminals and those who abuse government programs.

positions.summary: Supports a federal abortion ban, saying life begins at conception.
positions.quote: I support a federal abortion ban because I believe life begins at conception and that the right to life should be protected equally across state lines.

positions.summary: Supports deporting violent criminals and those abusing government programs, and removing welfare incentives for unlawful residency, while supporting a path to lawful residency for some who arrived as children.
positions.quote: We need a clear approach that starts with deporting violent criminals and those who abuse government programs. For others, we should remove incentives, like welfare benefits, that encourage illegal residency.

positions.summary: Supports constitutional carry and opposes legal hurdles to carrying a firearm.
positions.quote: States should not create burdensome legal hurdles just to carry a firearm.

positions.summary: Supports zoning reform limited to genuine infrastructure or pollution concerns, and opposes tax incentives that treat homes as investments rather than shelter.
positions.quote: Sound money would address much of this, but tax and zoning reform are also essential... Zoning should be limited to genuine infrastructure or pollution concerns.

positions.summary: Criticizes the influence of the Israel lobby (AIPAC) on U.S. politics as part of a broader call to register and restrict foreign agents' political influence.
positions.quote: A clear gap in the system is AIPAC, the Israel lobby, which has too much influence in our politics.

positions.summary: Supports ending government-backed health programs, including Social Security and government healthcare, in favor of a free-market approach.
positions.quote: End the Welfare State: End all welfare programs, including... Social Security, government healthcare, and government-backed mortgages. These programs create dependency, increase costs, and suppress wealth creation.

positions.summary: Supports abolishing the 16th Amendment (federal income tax) and property taxes in favor of user-based taxes and tariffs.
positions.quote: Property taxes should be illegal, and the 16th Amendment (income tax) should be abolished. America should rely on simpler, user-based taxes and tariffs.
